title: Passing the Integration Boost through to partners and end users is only a non-binding expectation
content:
A.2.2.9.2.2.1.1 states the intended economic path and then disclaims it in the same sentence: Integration Boost payments "are paid to the Prime Agent associated with the Integration Boost Partner... The **non-binding expectation** is that the Integration Boost amount is passed through from the Prime Agent to the Integration Boost Partner, and from the Integration Boost Partner to USDS users, providing those users with the equivalent of the Sky Savings Rate."

The purpose of the Primitive (A.2.2.9.2.1.1) is to give integrated USDS holders the Savings Rate. The mechanism pays a party two hops removed from those holders and requires nothing of either intermediary. A.2.2.9.2.2.1.4.3 confirms the same for the accompanying Distribution Reward: sharing with Integration Boost Partners "is subject to bilateral negotiation."

So the outcome the instrument exists to produce is left entirely to market behaviour. The theory is that competition supplies the enforcement — a partner that pockets the Boost instead of paying depositors loses deposits to one that passes it on — and that Sky prefers not to regulate its counterparties' pricing.

The risk is that neither hop faces competition in the relevant dimension. A Prime Agent negotiating with a partner protocol is a bilateral bargain, not a market; and end users cannot observe how much Boost their venue receives. Sky can therefore fund a yield subsidy whose incidence it cannot see, with no Atlas-level record of how much of it reaches the users the Primitive names as its beneficiaries.
description: The Boost is paid to the Prime Agent, and the two hops that would deliver Savings-Rate-equivalent yield to actual USDS users are explicitly unenforceable.
